<!-- Adapted to the sandbox's auto-generated cast (Kael/Merin) — see
     humor_at_climax.md's header note for why. -->
Kael counted the technique sequences twice, and twice they came out wrong
— not wrong the way a tired hand makes wrong, but wrong the way something
rewritten makes wrong, edges too clean where the ink should have bled.

The workshop was empty. It was supposed to be empty. Merin had the key
that night, not Kael, which meant someone else had let them in, or someone
else had never left.

Kael set the notes down without letting their hand shake, though it
wanted to. The door at the far end of the room — the one to the tool
cage, the one that was always locked — stood open a hand's width, lamplight
bleeding through the gap where there should have been none.

They had not opened that door tonight.

Kael's fingers found the wrapped bundle of old tools at their belt out of
pure habit, the way Merin always said they did when they were afraid and
didn't want to admit it. Whoever was on the other side of that door had
been careful enough to relock everything else in the shop and careless
enough — or confident enough — to leave that one thing open.

Kael understood, standing very still in the dark, that this was not
carelessness. It was a message. Someone wanted them to know they'd been
here.
